articles.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
articles.summary: As large language models (LLMs) are used in more and more new tasks, context engineering becomes a fundamental method to efficiently steer LLMs by constructing instruction prompts or metadata without intensive training. articles.title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion
articles.summary: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction.

articles.summary: When visual context makes an ordinary request unsafe to answer as asked, a blanket refusal may leave the user's need unresolved. articles.summary: A foundation model for time series is pretrained once and then asked to forecast series it has never seen, so the evidence for it is its score on held-out datasets. articles.title: Generation as Reverse Encoding
articles.summary: Pretrained visual representations accelerate generative learning by abstracting away appearance and spatial detail. Yet the same abstraction makes the return to pixels far harder, shifting much of the burden onto a larger decoder. We ask why the representation-to-pixel path should be learned independently when the encoder already provides a learned pixel-to-semantics path (the semantic encoding path). articles.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
articles.summary: AI agents now run statements against production databases, and several of the incidents that followed deleted production data, which came back only through backups or the provider's help. articles.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation

Yet recent findings show that vision foundation models already encode transferable detection knowledge, while further adaptation can impair generalization. articles.summary: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. articles.summary: Structured clinical decisions from volumetric computed tomography (CT) require anatomically grounded predictions and calibrated confidence estimates. articles.summary: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. articles.summary: Agents in complex, stochastic environments must contend with dynamics that can exceed their world models' predictive capacity and randomness that obscure the consequences of their actions. articles.summary: Generating coherent and explorable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap is a fundamental and long-standing challenge in computer vision, which existing geometry-aware methods fail to address. articles.summary: After a large language model (LLM) agent generates an artifact, users often send edit requests for it. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. articles.summary: Autoresearch agents, which autonomously design, run, and refine experiments, are accelerating scientific progress, particularly in AI research. articles.summary: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). articles.summary: Recent self-improving coding agents have achieved strong benchmark performance by iteratively modifying their own executable implementations. articles.summary: Video world models for robots are increasingly conditioned on a simulated or rendered proxy of the scene, on the assumption that the video will show what the proxy shows. articles.summary: Decision models are language models fine-tuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. articles.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
articles.summary: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often yields all-fail groups on long-horizon agent tasks: every sampled trajectory receives zero reward, leaving group-relative methods without a reward-based policy gradient. articles.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
articles.summary: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. articles.title: Let Vision-Language Models Generate Images through Their Representations
articles.summary: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. articles.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
articles.summary: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. articles.title: Speak When You See It: Proactive Task Assistants Should Wait for Evidence, Not the Clock

articles.summary: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks.
